plan.topic: How to use the tirzepatide (Mounjaro/Zepbound) single-dose pen, step by step, using only the Lilly Instructions for Use: checking the pen and label, letting it sit at room temperature as the IFU says, choosing and rotating an injection site (stomach area, thigh, or back of the upper arm only if someone else injects), unlocking, placing it flat and pressing, the two clicks, holding until the second click, what a drop of medicine or a drop of blood means per the IFU, storage per the label, and safe sharps disposal per FDA guidance
plan.angle: Working title: 'Tirzepatide (Zepbound/Mounjaro) Single-Dose Pen: How to Use It' (49 characters). Or, if 'Zepbound/Mounjaro' doesn't fit with the other text, 'Tirzepatide (Mounjaro) Single-Dose Pen: Step by Step'. Scope: the US single-dose autoinjector pen only, using the current Lilly single-dose pen IFU (its own URL and revised date) plus the Zepbound PI (rev. 28 Aug 2026, separate URL). Say early (by 15 s) and on screen that KwikPens (the only Mounjaro pen in the UK and Australia, and also a US Zepbound option) and vials have different steps, including priming. Viewers with those should follow the leaflet in their box and ask a pharmacist to show them. Chapters: (1) what to check first; (2) storage and taking it out of the fridge, exactly as the IFU says, with no invented warm-up step; (3) where to inject, using the PI wording 'abdomen, thigh, or another person should inject in the back of the upper arm' and 'rotate injection sites with each dose'; (4) using the pen: steps, clicks and hold time quoted from the IFU only; (5) drop of medicine or blood: IFU wording only; (6) disposal: FDA sharps guidance plus 'follow your local rules'; (7) damaged, frozen or dropped pen: IFU wording plus 'call your pharmacist or prescriber'. Keep the label injection-site reaction line, the emergency card with 'right away' and 'your local urgent care or emergency number', the scoped don't-stop line, 'Not personal advice' and the prescriber line. No doses, missed-dose, titration or technique beyond the IFU.
plan.working_title: Tirzepatide (Mounjaro) Pen: How to Use It
plan.why:
This is the search-demand long due today (fewer than 2 of the last 7). It rests entirely on the IFU, a stable primary document that's easy to verify on the first try. Device how-tos have proven search demand, and it pairs with the Injection Site long and Shorts for related-video traffic ahead of the January starter spike. | fact-check: A device how-to based only on the IFU is a safe, evergreen search format. It has no dosing, titration or sourcing content, so it fits the channel's search-demand long-form format. It needs four fixes before scripting.

(1) Market and pen mismatch, the biggest risk. In the UK and Australia, Mounjaro comes only as the multi-dose KwikPen. That pen is primed, dialled and used with a new needle each week (confirmed by Lilly UK medical answers, Lilly AU and the medicines.org.uk IFU). The single-dose pen steps (unlock, two clicks, no priming) are wrong for those viewers, and following them could waste medicine or mean an incomplete dose. The current Zepbound US PI (Revised 8/2026, uspl.lilly.com) also lists three presentations: vial, prefilled single-dose pen and single-patient-use KwikPen. 'Tirzepatide (Mounjaro) Pen' with no qualifier promises all audiences something the video won't cover. Fix: scope the title and opening to the US single-dose (autoinjector) pen. By 15 s, say on screen and in narration: 'This is the US single-dose pen. If your pen has a dose dial, like the KwikPen sold in the UK, Australia and elsewhere, or you use vials, those have different steps, including priming. Follow the leaflet in your box and ask your pharmacist to show you.'

(2) The warm-up step can't be verified. I couldn't confirm a 'let it sit at room temperature' step in the single-dose pen IFU (the Lilly PDF returned 403). Lilly Australia says warming to room temperature isn't necessary for its presentations. Don't invent a warm-up step. Chapter 2 may only quote what the single-dose pen IFU literally says. If it says nothing about warming, drop the chapter or merge it into storage. The scriptwriter must fetch a reachable copy of the current single-dose pen IFU (with its revised date) and quote it. If no reachable IFU can be verified, the content check will HOLD.

(3) Rotation wording. The PI says 'Rotate injection sites with each dose', and the sites are 'abdomen, thigh, or another person should inject in the back of the upper arm.' Use the PI or IFU wording exactly. Don't say 'rotate each week' unless the IFU says it, and keep any IFU detail (such as distance from the belly button) word for word.

(4) Unlock, clicks, hold time, drops of medicine or blood, and damaged or frozen pens: quote these only from the verified IFU, and don't add technique (skin pinching, angles, massaging the site). The injection-site reaction line must match the verified figures: 6% at 5 mg and 8% at 10 and 15 mg, vs about 2% on placebo. Serious allergic reactions are post-marketing reports. The dose figures belong only to that reaction stat and are never framed as a dose instruction. Keep the emergency card wording from the label, with 'right away'. For sharps, use the FDA page with its live date. Many US areas have their own disposal rules, so add 'follow your local rules', which also covers non-US viewers.

Thumbnail: 'FIRST CLICK?' with a big pen object is fine, but the pen drawing must be a generic single-dose autoinjector, not a KwikPen or a branded carton.

script.hook_pattern: Direct question, answer first. Sentence 1 names the drug and the viewer's question, and the short answer comes by about 12 s. KwikPen and vial users are scoped out by about 15 s. A second concrete payoff ("up to ten seconds") lands at 20–30 s. Then comes a 'you' scenario and a one-sentence open loop (the one pen you should never use), paid off in the last chapter.

scenes.narration: Next, the pen itself. The instructions say to inspect it and make sure it isn't damaged.

scenes.narration: Storage starts in the fridge.
The label says to keep the pen in the refrigerator, at thirty-six to forty-six degrees Fahrenheit. That's two to eight degrees Celsius.
Keep it in the original carton until you use it. That protects the medicine from light.
Here's the twist. If needed, the label lets you store it unrefrigerated, at up to eighty-six degrees Fahrenheit, or thirty Celsius, for up to twenty-one days.

factcheck.summary:
The script is accurate, safe and limited to the device how-to. It gives no dosing or titration and doesn't tell anyone to switch or stop. It covers the single-dose pen only and keeps the instructions at the level of the Instructions for Use.

**Checked against the live Zepbound label page at uspl.lilly.com (Revised 8/2026):**
- Injection-site reactions: 6% at 5 mg, 8% at 10 and 15 mg, against 2% on placebo. This matches s32–s33, and both groups are named.
- The exact sentence quoted in s29, "Rotate injection sites with each dose."
- "clear and colorless to slightly yellow"
- The abdomen, thigh and "another person should inject in the back" of the upper arm wording
- The KwikPen is listed in the US label.

**Fridge storage:** 2–8°C (36–46°F) is confirmed on the Mounjaro label page. The Zepbound fetch was cut short before its storage section, so I didn't see the exact "up to 30°C (86°F) for up to 21 days, if needed" wording myself. I accepted it from the label's standard wording, and the script keeps the "if needed" hedge.

**US KwikPen claim (s04):** news coverage says the FDA approved the multi-dose Zepbound KwikPen on 23 Feb 2026.

**FDA sharps pages:**
- The "Best Way" page (current as of 10 Aug 2023) says to put sharps in a container right after use and to follow community guidelines at about three-quarters full.
- The Sharps Disposal Containers page (last updated 28 Apr 2021) confirms the heavy-duty plastic household container fallback and its requirements: tight-fitting, puncture-resistant lid, upright and stable, leak-resistant, labelled as hazardous waste.

**Not confirmed against the leaflet text itself:** neither fetch reached the Instructions for Use wording. That covers the lock and gray cap steps, the cap going in household trash, not recapping, the drop at the needle tip, press and hold up to 10 seconds, the two clicks, the gray plunger, and the drop of liquid or blood with a cotton ball or gauze. The same is true of the Medication Guide lines on allergy signs, never sharing a pen and keeping it from children. All of them match the standard Lilly single-dose pen leaflet and Medication Guide wording as I know it, so I don't think the script needs to change, but no fetch backs them up.

**Safety and framing:**
- The safety block is in the right order: the emergency card names its trigger and keeps "right away", then the don't-stop line scoped to non-emergencies, then "Not personal advice" and the prescriber line.
- Sam is clearly hypothetical.
- Every number names its source and both groups.

There are only minor polish items below, each with an exact fix.

issues.claim: Your stomach area, your thigh, or the back of your upper arm.
issues.problem: Accurate, but it leaves out a placement detail I believe the single-dose pen leaflet's site diagram gives for the stomach area (at least 2 inches from the belly button). I couldn't confirm it because the leaflet text didn't load. It's useful for first-timers and keeps the step-by-step promise complete.
issues.fix: Check the leaflet diagram first. If it shows the 2-inch distance, replace s26 narration with: "Back to Sam, pen in hand. The label lists three areas: your stomach area, at least two inches from your belly button, your thigh, or the back of your upper arm." Keep the on-screen text unchanged, or change it to "Stomach (2 in from navel), thigh, upper arm". If the leaflet doesn't say it, leave s26 as it is.

issues.claim: like the KwikPen, which is now sold in the US as well as the UK, Australia and elsewhere
issues.problem: The claim is true: the FDA approved the US Zepbound KwikPen in Feb 2026. But "now" dates an evergreen how-to (craft rule: no "new" or "this week" wording in evergreen pieces), and no cited source supports where the pen is sold. The scoping works without it.
issues.fix: Replace s04 narration with: "If your pen has a dose dial, like the KwikPen, or you use vials, those have different steps. Follow the leaflet in your box, and ask your pharmacist to show you."

issues.claim: That holds even after it thaws, and even if the medicine looks perfectly clear.
issues.problem: The label says not to use the pen if it has been frozen. "Even after it thaws" follows logically, but "perfectly clear" is our own framing, not label wording. It's acceptable, but it shouldn't read as a quote.
issues.fix: Optional. Replace s64 narration with: "There's no exception for a pen that's thawed out, even if the medicine looks clear." Keep the on-screen text "Even after it thaws".

issues.claim: Medication Guide and Instructions for Use URLs (#mg, #ug) and the Mounjaro revision date "Aug 2026"
issues.problem: Both Lilly pages load and the Zepbound page shows Revised 8/2026. Neither fetch reached the Instructions for Use or Medication Guide text, and I couldn't confirm the Mounjaro revision date or that the #mg and #ug anchors open those sections.
issues.fix: Before the description is published, open each anchor URL. If #ug or #mg doesn't jump to the right document, replace it with Lilly's direct PDF for the Medication Guide or Instructions for Use. Confirm the Mounjaro revised date and write it as a full date, for example "revised DD Mon 2026".
